explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD tells Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites." (Numbers 6:23) Moses is the middleman here, and Aaron and his sons are the ones who get the words to say. The blessing itself is for the Israelites. Passing along a message without changing a word is a real skill, and I've seen people mess up a simple grocery list.

Good guess, but the text doesn't send this one to the elders. The LORD says, "Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites." (Numbers 6:23) Aaron and his sons are the ones getting the words. The elders aren't in this passage at all, so they can relax.

Joshua and Caleb are the two spies who trusted God in Numbers 14:6-9, but they're not in this passage. Here the LORD tells Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites." (Numbers 6:23) So the words go to Aaron and his sons, and the Israelites are the ones who get blessed. Nice try, baker. Those two are great names to have in your corner.

Right on, baker. God's instruction is "Say to them…" and then He gives the words. (Numbers 6:23) So this blessing is meant to be spoken out loud. No paperwork, no engraving, just Aaron and his sons saying it to the Israelites.

Doorposts do show up elsewhere in the Bible, like Deuteronomy 6:9, but not here. In this passage God says, "Say to them…" and then gives the words of the blessing. (Numbers 6:23) Nothing in these verses tells Aaron and his sons to write anything. Good news for them, because that's a LOT of doors.

Stone tablets are a real thing in the Bible, like in Exodus 24:12, but they're not what this passage says. God tells Aaron and his sons to "Say to them…" and then gives the blessing. (Numbers 6:23) So it's spoken, not carved. I'd say no chisels needed, and my mustache is relieved on their behalf.

That's it, baker. Line two says, "…may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you…" (Numbers 6:25) The shining face and the grace come together in one line. I think that's a warm thing to hear spoken over you.

Not quite, baker. Stern is a face with its arms crossed, and this line pictures the opposite. The LORD's face shines on His people, and the line goes on to ask that He "…be gracious to you…" (Numbers 6:25) I think that's the difference between walking into a room where someone lights up and walking into one where someone checks their watch. This blessing is the lighting up.

Not this time, baker. Hidden would be a face turned away, and this line asks for the reverse: that the LORD "…cause His face to shine upon you…" (Numbers 6:25) Picture a porch light left on for you. That's the kind of welcome the words are asking for, and it comes with the second request, "…and be gracious to you…" So the answer is gracious, not hidden.

Yes, baker, true. Look at the verbs: "May the LORD bless you and keep you…" then "…may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you…" then "…may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace." (Numbers 6:24-26) Every line starts with the LORD and what He does. The blessing is all about Him giving.

This one is actually true, so let's look at the text. Every line starts with "May the LORD…" and then says what He does: bless, keep, shine, be gracious, lift up His countenance, give peace. (Numbers 6:24-26) There's no line asking the people to do anything. It's all the LORD giving, baker.

Yes, baker. God says, "So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them." (Numbers 6:27) When Aaron and his sons speak the blessing, they're putting God's name on His people. It's a big moment, and it happens just by speaking the words.

A crown sounds fancy, but it isn't what the text says. God says, "So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them." (Numbers 6:27) The thing being put on the people is His name. No crown required, baker.

A robe is a good guess if you're thinking priest clothes, but that's not what the verse says. God says, "So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them." (Numbers 6:27) What goes on the people is His name. The blessing doesn't come with a wardrobe change.

Close, but the last words of the passage say otherwise. God says, "So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them." (Numbers 6:27) Aaron and his sons speak the words and put God's name on the people, and God says, "…I will bless them." The blessing is His to give, baker.

That's right, baker. Aaron and his sons speak the words and put God's name on the Israelites, but God says, "…I will bless them." (Numbers 6:27) The priests are the ones who say the blessing, and God is the One who says He will bless His people.
